verses.text: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said, “Strike the tops of the pillars, that the thresholds may shake; and break them in pieces on the head of all of them; and I will kill the last of them with the sword: there shall not one of them flee away, and there shall not one of them escape.
Though they dig into Sheol,  there my hand will take them; and though they climb up to heaven, there I will bring them down.

Though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them out there; and though they be hidden from my sight in the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
Though they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. I will set my eyes on them for evil, and not for good.
For the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, is he who touches the land and it melts, and all who dwell in it will mourn; and it will rise up wholly like the River, and will sink again, like the River of Egypt.
It is he who builds his rooms in the heavens, and has founded his vault on the earth; he who calls for the waters of the sea, and pours them out on the surface of the earth; Yahweh is his name.

Are you not like the children of the Ethiopians to me, children of Israel?” says Yahweh. “Haven’t I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?
Behold, the eyes of the Lord Yahweh are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the surface of the earth; except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” says Yahweh.
“For, behold, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet not the least kernel will fall on the earth.
All the sinners of my people will die by the sword, who say, ‘Evil won’t overtake nor meet us.’
In that day I will raise up the tent of David who is fallen, and close up its breaches, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old;
that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and all the nations who are called by my name,” says Yahweh who does this.
“Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the one treading grapes him who sows seed; and sweet wine will drip from the mountains, and flow from the hills.

I will bring my people Israel back from captivity, and they will rebuild the ruined cities, and inhabit them; and they will plant vineyards, and drink wine from them. They shall also make gardens, and eat their fruit.
I will plant them on their land, and they will no more be plucked up out of their land which I have given them,” says Yahweh your God.

footnotes.content: Even in a vision of judgment, the Lord stands — not hidden, not absent, but *at the altar* where mercy meets justice. I've learned that God's severity toward sin is not indifference; it is the love of a Father who will not let us cling to what destroys us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sheol or heaven — there is nowhere to hide from the Lord's gaze. Not to terrorize us, but to remind us that grace reaches farther than our shame ever could. We are known, seen, and yet claimed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The top of Carmel and the sea's bottom — Amos sweeps from the mountain of fertility to the abyss. Nothing in creation offers refuge from the Creator. Yet as I've grown older, I see this not as threat but as the foundation of trust: the same God who is inescapable is the one who loved us first.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The hardest line in this vision: "I will set my eyes on them for evil, and not for good." Yet even this judgment is *His* hand at work — not chaos, but the discipline of the God who refuses to abandon His people to their own ruin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Nile River — Egypt's lifeblood — rises and falls in patterns Israel watched their whole history. Now the God of all waters moves not only the Nile but the very ground. Creation itself bends to His touch; how much more does He care for His children.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The One who builds rooms in heaven and vaults upon earth — who commands the sea itself — is not distant majesty but the God of architecture and order, the One who knows the shape of things. In my years, I've seen how this power works not for display but for preservation of all He loves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The Ethiopians to me" — what a turn. The Lord brings Egypt, Caphtor, and Kir into the same account as Israel. Israel is not uniquely favored for special treatment but equally accountable. Yet in this equality lies a deeper truth: God's grace to *all nations* flows from the same fountain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The eyes of the Lord are on the sinful kingdom — for destruction, not protection. Yet watch: "except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob." Even in wrath, the *except* arrives. The God of judgment is the God who always leaves room for a remnant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sieve separates the chaff from the grain, and the grain stays. The Lord's sifting among the nations is not arbitrary loss but the separation of what endures from what cannot. The covenant people will be scattered but not destroyed — a hard mercy, yet mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Evil won't overtake nor meet us" — how many times I have heard confident denial mask spiritual blindness. The sinners die because they refused to see what was already moving toward them. Honesty before the Lord, even about our smallness, is the first breath of freedom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The tent of David fallen — the dynasty broken. Yet the Lord promises *not a new throne* but a *restored one*, in its ancient form. There is deep gospel here: restoration does not mean the forgetting of wounds, but the healing that remembers what was broken and holds it whole again.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even Edom — the brother nation, the old rival — is included in the restoration. What was scattered comes under one rule again. The humility of a returning people is that they inherit not conquest but reconciliation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The plowman overtakes the reaper — abundance so great the harvest never ends before the next planting begins. Sweet wine drips from mountains. These are not fantasies but the language of a God who loves *joy*, who delights in His people's feasting and rest as much as their repentance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Captivity reversed: people return, cities are rebuilt, vineyards planted, gardens made. After judgment comes labor, but it is *their* labor in *their* land. The God of restoration is not a God of shortcuts; He calls His people back to the work of building homes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "They will no more be plucked up out of their land" — readers today hear an echo in how the God who once spoke this to Israel continues to hold fast to His people through every upheaval and scattering. The promise is not that the land will never be threatened, but that *His grip* will never loosen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
